newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's bourse watchdog taxes trade to pay costs.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's bourse watchdog taxes trade to pay costs.

text.p: Morocco's stock exchange watchdog Conseil Deontologique des Valeurs Mobilieres (CDVM) has started imposing two taxes on bourse transactions to pay for its own operations, a CDVM spokesman said on Monday.
"The CDVM is taking 0.04 percent on share trading and 0.02 percent on bond transactions because it needs money to do its job properly as a control body," the spokesman said.
He said the decision followed a decree on June 30 stating that from July 1, the CDVM will benefit from two taxes described as "a parafiscal tax for the stock exchange control."
The CDVM was set up in 1994 and had been up to now funded by commissions on public issues and on mutual funds, plus state subsidies, he said.
Among other aspects of its work, it has delisted 18 companies for not publishing their annual results.
At present, 48 stocks are listed on the exchange.
